title: How to Optimize Content for AI Search: Write Passages Engines Can Quote
metaTitle: How to Optimize Content for AI Search: 8 Steps (2026)
metaDescription: Optimize content for AI search by making every section a quotable answer: lead with the answer, add sourced numbers, name your entities and keep facts current.
primaryKeyword: how to optimize content for ai search
shortAnswer: Optimize the passage, not just the page. Open every section with a self-contained 40–60 word answer, back it with sourced numbers and attributed quotes, state entity facts plainly, and keep dated facts current. Publish one page per question. Schema cannot replace text worth quoting, and Google says its AI features need no special markup.
intro:
AI engines do not read a page the way a visitor does. They retrieve passages, check whether one can stand alone, and quote it with a link. Optimizing for AI search is therefore editorial work: make each section a complete, checkable answer.

We label each claim documented (an engine's docs say so), measured (a study found it) or our judgment. Google's [own guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) calls optimizing for its AI features "still SEO"; for ChatGPT search, Perplexity and Claude we found crawler rules but no content guide, so research and judgment carry more weight.

sections.heading: What does optimizing content for AI search mean?
sections.body:
Optimizing content for AI search (called AEO or GEO, sometimes AI content optimization) means making a passage of your page easy to retrieve, trust and quote inside a generated answer. Two gates apply: eligibility (can the engine fetch the page?) and selection (which eligible passage gets quoted?). Content work pays off at the second gate.

**Eligibility is documented, and usually fine.** Google needs a page [indexed and snippet-eligible](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide). OpenAI says sites [opted out of OAI-SearchBot](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) do not appear in ChatGPT search answers; [Perplexity](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots) and [Anthropic](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler) say similar. In [AEOeye's crawler access study](/blog/ai-crawler-user-agent-directory) (October 2026; 391 well-known sites, a convenience sample), 1 of 193 SaaS sites blocked any AI retrieval bot in robots.txt, yet 24 of 88 e-commerce and consumer homepages challenged our crawler, so check firewall rules too.

**Selection works on passages.** Google's AI features are [rooted in its core ranking systems](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), which include a [passage ranking system](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ranking-systems-guide) for individual sections, and use [retrieval-augmented generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retrieval-augmented_generation) plus query fan-out, related searches on sub-topics. The original [RAG paper](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2005.11401) indexed 100-word chunks; ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude publish no chunk sizes, so write sections that survive being lifted out.

sections.heading: Does an answer-first structure get you quoted?
sections.body:
Probably. A 2025 [retrieval study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13950) found dense embedding and ColBERT-style models lose 15.6% of performance on average when the relevant information appears later in a passage; BM25 and rerankers were more robust. We found no direct test on ChatGPT or Perplexity, so this is mechanism, not proof.

Engines lift short spans, so the first sentence under each heading should answer that heading in 40–60 words and make sense alone. The length is our rule of thumb, not an engine limit. Anthropic's web search tool [returns up to 150 characters of cited text](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool) per citation, about one sentence. Two habits help:

- **Name the subject.** Skip "it", "this approach" and "as mentioned above"; a lifted passage loses its neighbours.
- **Phrase headings as questions.** [Pew Research](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found AI summaries on 53% of Google searches of 10+ words but 8% of one- or two-word searches (March 2025).

This does not mean chopping a page into fragments: Google says there is [no requirement to break content into tiny pieces](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide).

sections.heading: Which content elements make AI engines quote you?
sections.body:
The best-measured elements are statistics, quotations and citations of credible sources. In the [GEO study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735) (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024), each lifted a rewritten page's visibility by 30–40% on one metric and 15–30% on another, while keyword stuffing gave little to no improvement.

The [setup](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09735v3): 10,000 queries; a research engine on GPT-3.5-turbo answering from the top five Google results; one source per query rewritten by an LLM and compared with its original.

The limits: a 2023 research engine, not Google's AI features or today's chatbots, measuring share within an answer, not retrieval. Google's guide never mentions these tactics; it says unique, [non-commodity content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) will likely matter more than any other suggestion in it. Read the study as evidence for credibility, not a formula.

What to do:

- Put a real number, its source and its date in one sentence ([anatomy of a quotable passage](/answers/what-makes-content-quotable-by-ai)).
- Attribute quotes to the person who said them, and link primary sources.
- Add what only you have: your data, pricing and first-hand tests. Never let a tool invent a figure.

sections.heading: Does schema markup help AI search?
sections.body:
Schema markup helps machines parse a page and tell entities apart; it is not a citation switch and cannot replace quotable text. As of October 2026, Google says structured data [is not required](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) for its AI features and no special markup is needed. Use it because it is accurate and cheap; [structured data for AI](/blog/structured-data-for-ai) covers types and examples.

- **Correlation exists.** [GEO-16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10762), an observational study of 1,100 cited B2B SaaS pages, found metadata and freshness, semantic HTML and structured data most associated with citation. Its authors warn that confounders such as brand reputation may explain this.
- **FAQPage is no longer a Google rich result.** Google [stopped showing](https://developers.google.com/search/updates) it on May 7, 2026. Write FAQs for readers.
- **Adoption is not effect.** In the [same study](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv), Organization markup was on 129 of 176 SaaS homepages (73.3%): table stakes. FAQPage was on 13 (7.4%), but on 18 of 42 AI-visibility tool vendors (42.9%, aeoeye.com included). That shows what the AEO industry believes, not what works.
- **llms.txt follows the same logic.** [The proposed file](https://llmstxt.org/) is on 108 of 180 checkable SaaS sites (60%), Google says it [ignores such files](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), and we know of no major engine documenting its use for answers. See [what is llms.txt](/blog/what-is-llms-txt).

sections.heading: How should you structure a page for AI?
sections.body:
Build the page as a stack of self-contained answers: a short answer first, one question per heading, tables where facts run in parallel. In the last column, Documented means an engine's docs say so, Measured means a published study found it, and Judgment means the call is ours. For a fuller audit, use our [AEO audit checklist](/blog/aeo-audit-checklist).

| Check | What to do | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fetchable | Allow OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot and Googlebot; check firewall logs; keep answer text in server-sent HTML | Documented, Judgment |
| Short answers | Each H2 is the buyer's question, answered in 40–60 words, plus a takeaways box | Judgment |
| Sourced proof | Number, unit, date and source in one sentence; attributed quotes | Measured |
| Entity facts | One brand and product name everywhere; price, audience and location in plain sentences; [Organization markup](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization) with sameAs | Judgment, Documented |
| Tables and lists | Parallel facts in labelled rows, so a lifted row keeps its labels | Judgment |
| Dates | A visible "Last updated" that [matches dateModified](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/publication-dates) | Documented, Measured |

![Three white jigsaw pieces joined together with one loose piece beside them on a blue background.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/5505122/pexels-photo-5505122.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: Should you use AI tools to optimize content?
sections.body:
Yes for structure, editing and gap-finding; no for facts. "AI content optimization" also names this other job; only optimizing for AI engines decides whether they quote you. Google says generative AI can help with research and [adding structure to original content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content).

- **Good uses:** restructuring a draft answer-first, listing sub-questions it leaves unanswered and tightening sentences.
- **Bad uses:** inventing statistics, quotes or sources (models [predict likely words rather than retrieve facts](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content), so any figure a tool adds is a guess until you source it), and mass-producing pages, which Google says may violate its scaled content abuse policy.

sections.heading: How does this change your AI content strategy?
sections.body:
Publish fewer, better pages: one strong page per buyer question, with sub-questions as sections rather than near-duplicate pages. Google says a high quantity of pages does not make a site more relevant and warns against separate pages for every query variation or [fan-out query](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide). If two pages would answer the same buyer prompt, they are one page.

On 2026-09-24 we retired 234 of our blog posts and merged 27 duplicates, after Search Console showed about half of our 496 posts were unrelated to AI visibility and had no clicks in 90 days. On 2026-10-03 we merged another 165 duplicate-intent and research pages into 42; this guide replaces five of them. It is our position, not a measured result: the merges are days old and we have no citation data yet.

- **Give readers a reason to click.** [Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2025/07/22/google-users-are-less-likely-to-click-on-links-when-an-ai-summary-appears-in-the-results/) found Google users clicked a regular result in 8% of visits when an AI summary appeared, against 15% when none did. Answer first, then offer what a summary cannot: your data, a tool, the full comparison.
- **Measure by asking.** Re-ask the same buyer questions monthly. Google's [Search Console report](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports) counts impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode, and our [free audit](/) asks three buyer questions to ChatGPT.

![Two colleagues at a table review printed forms next to a tablet showing a chart.](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8171198/pexels-photo-8171198.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

keyTakeaways: Optimize the passage: open each section with a self-contained 40–60 word answer, proof beneath.
Sourced statistics, attributed quotes and cited sources are the best-measured levers (30–40% in the 2023 GEO study).
Google says its AI features need no special markup; schema cannot replace quotable text.
Use AI tools for structure and editing, never for facts.
Publish one page per buyer question; re-test the same questions monthly.

faqs.a: It names two jobs. One is optimizing content for AI engines: writing sections that ChatGPT search, Perplexity, Claude and Google's AI features can retrieve, trust and quote. The other is using AI tools to research, draft and edit. Only the first decides whether engines name you; the second changes how fast you produce pages and still needs a human to check every fact.

faqs.q: Does schema markup help AI search visibility?
faqs.a: Not as a lever on its own. As of October 2026, Google says structured data is not required for its AI features and no special schema.org markup is needed. Markup still helps machines identify your organization and describe visible content accurately, so keep it correct. It cannot substitute for a clear, sourced answer in the text, which is what an engine actually quotes.

faqs.q: How long should an answer-first opening be?
faqs.a: Aim for 40 to 60 words that answer the heading's question and make sense alone. That is our rule of thumb, not an engine limit. Anthropic's web search tool, for example, returns up to 150 characters of cited text per citation, roughly one sentence, so put the core claim in the first sentence and the supporting detail after it.

faqs.q: Will optimizing for AI search hurt my Google rankings?
faqs.a: No. Google calls optimizing for its AI features still SEO and names a clear technical structure and unique, valuable content as the foundation. The habit to drop is keyword stuffing, which gave little to no improvement in the GEO study. Write for readers first: the section that answers a buyer clearly is also the one an engine can quote.

faqs.q: How do I know whether AI engines quote my content?
faqs.a: Ask your buyers' questions in each engine, several times each because answers vary, and log whether you are named, cited and described correctly. For Google, Search Console's generative AI performance report shows impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode by page. AEOeye's free audit asks three unbranded buyer questions to ChatGPT; the $29 full report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity.

definitions.definition: Optimizing content so generative AI engines surface and cite it. The term was formalized by Aggarwal et al. (2023), who built a benchmark to test content changes; answer engine optimization (AEO) names the same practice.
A technique that lets a language model retrieve and incorporate information from external sources before it answers.

A set of concurrent, related searches an AI model generates to gather more results for one user question, for example splitting a lawn-care question into herbicide, chemical-free and prevention searches.
A writing structure that puts the most important information first and the detail after it, also called bottom line up front (BLUF).
A standardized format for giving a search engine information about a page and classifying its content; Google recommends JSON-LD for it.

howToSteps.name: List the ten questions your buyers ask
howToSteps.text: Pull them from sales calls, support tickets and Search Console queries. Ask each one in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Mode three or more times, and record whether you are named, cited and described correctly. That is your baseline.

howToSteps.name: Confirm the engines can fetch you
howToSteps.text: Check robots.txt for OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot and Googlebot, then look for firewall or CDN challenges in your logs. Blocking a training bot such as GPTBot is a separate decision and does not remove you from ChatGPT search.

howToSteps.name: Rewrite each section opening as a self-contained answer
howToSteps.text: Make the heading the buyer's question and the first 40-60 words the complete answer. Name the product or company instead of writing it or this, and cut as mentioned above. Keep the rest of the section as proof, not preamble.

howToSteps.name: Attach proof to every claim
howToSteps.text: Give each number a unit, a date and a source in the same sentence. Attribute quotes to the person who said them and link primary sources. Delete any claim you cannot source, and never let a tool supply figures or quotes.

howToSteps.name: State entity facts plainly
howToSteps.text: Use one brand and product name everywhere. Say what the product is, who it is for, what it costs and where you operate in plain sentences, and keep them identical across your site and your profiles on review sites and directories.

howToSteps.name: Add schema only where it matches the page
howToSteps.text: Use Organization with sameAs links on the homepage, Product or SoftwareApplication with Offer where you sell something, and Article with dates on guides. Mark up only what is visible, write it as JSON-LD and validate it. Google does not require any of it for its AI features.

howToSteps.name: Merge duplicates and date what remains
howToSteps.text: Give each question one page and 301-redirect near-duplicates into it. Show a visible last-updated date that matches your dateModified markup, and refresh prices, features and statistics when they change. Leave the date alone on pages whose content has not.

howToSteps.name: Re-ask the same questions and compare
howToSteps.text: After engines have had time to re-crawl, repeat the baseline with the same questions and several runs each, and check Search Console's generative AI performance report for Google. For daily monitoring across hundreds of prompts, dedicated trackers such as Profound, Peec AI or Otterly are built for it; AEOeye is a snapshot, not a daily tracker.
